items.stem:

Ransomware attacks lock or encrypt data until a ransom is paid. Cybercrimes can be committed from anywhere in the world, which creates problems of jurisdiction."

items.answer: (i) The virtual environment created by connected computers and networks, including the internet. (ii) Fraudsters use them to take over accounts and steal money through phishing and identity theft. (iii) The conclusion is wrong: Phishing means tricking people into giving personal information through fake messages or websites.
items.markingKey: 1+1+1 marks: (i) The virtual environment created by connected computers and networks, including the internet. items.stem: "PIL is called a tool of social justice." Examine this statement with reference to the judiciary and public interest litigation.

items.stem:
Study the extract below and answer the questions.
"The Uniform Civil Code is a Directive Principle and is not enforceable by courts. Opponents argue that a Uniform Civil Code may affect the freedom of religion and cultural diversity of minorities. Hindu personal law was codified in 1955-56 by the Hindu Marriage Act, the Hindu Succession Act, the Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act and the Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act. India has different personal laws for Hindus, Muslims, Christians and Parsis."
(i) Explain the term 'Uniform Civil Code', which is related to the theme of the extract. (1)
(ii) Using the extract and your own knowledge, explain the following: Many argue for a Uniform Civil Code on grounds of gender justice. (1)
(iii) A student concludes: "The Uniform Civil Code is a Fundamental Right." Use your knowledge of the chapter to evaluate this conclusion. (1)
items.answer: (i) A single set of civil laws on family matters applicable to all citizens irrespective of religion. (ii) Several personal-law rules have treated women unequally in marriage, divorce and succession. (iii) The conclusion is wrong: It is a Directive Principle under Article 44 and is not justiciable.
items.markingKey: 1+1+1 marks: (i) A single set of civil laws on family matters applicable to all citizens irrespective of religion. (ii) Several personal-law rules have treated women unequally in marriage, divorce and succession. (iii) The conclusion is wrong: It is a Directive Principle under Article 44 and is not justiciable.

items.stem:
Study the extract below and answer the questions.
"External sovereignty means that the state is free from the control of other states. Jean Bodin defined sovereignty as supreme power over citizens and subjects, unrestrained by law. Pluralists argue that associations such as churches, trade unions and professional bodies also command loyalty, so sovereignty is shared. In India, sovereignty ultimately rests with the people, as the Preamble begins with 'We, the people of India'."
(i) Explain the term 'internal sovereignty', which is related to the theme of the extract. (1)
(ii) Using the extract and your own knowledge, explain the following: A colony is not regarded as a sovereign state. (1)
(iii) A student concludes: "External sovereignty refers to the supremacy of the state over associations within it." Use your knowledge of the chapter to evaluate this conclusion. (1)
items.answer: (i) The supreme authority of the state over all persons and associations within its territory. (ii) It lacks external sovereignty because it is controlled by a foreign power. (iii) The conclusion is wrong: That is internal sovereignty; external sovereignty is freedom from foreign control.
items.markingKey: 1+1+1 marks: (i) The supreme authority of the state over all persons and associations within its territory. (ii) It lacks external sovereignty because it is controlled by a foreign power. (iii) The conclusion is wrong: That is internal sovereignty; external sovereignty is freedom from foreign control.

items.stem:
Arrange the following in chronological order (earliest first):
